title: The Lost Subways of North America

sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: If you've spent any amount of time driving through any major American city,
sentences.zh: 如果你曾花时间开车穿过任何一个美国主要城市，

sentences.en: you know what it's like to be stuck in bumper-to-bumper traffic.
sentences.zh: 你就会知道在水泄不通的车流中动弹不得是什么滋味。

sentences.en: The experience of crawling along, listening to people honking,
sentences.zh: 那种龟速挪动、听着此起彼伏的喇叭声，

sentences.en: and feeling your soul leaving your body.
sentences.zh: 以及感觉灵魂正被抽离身体的体验。

sentences.en: But no one, no one understands this pain better than someone from Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 但没有人、没有人比洛杉矶人更能体会这种痛苦。

sentences.en: I got stuck in traffic on the 101 freeway through Hollywood,
sentences.zh: 我有次在穿过好莱坞的101号高速公路上堵得水泄不通，

sentences.en: and I was thinking to myself,
what am I doing behind this guy in a Jeep with too many bumper stickers,
sentences.zh: 我为什么非要跟在一辆贴满车贴的吉普车后面，

sentences.en: and why hasn't my car moved for half an hour?
sentences.zh: 而且我的车为什么半小时了都没动一下？

sentences.en: He used to live in L.A.,
so he understands this struggle all too well.
sentences.zh: 所以他对这种挣扎感同身受。

sentences.en: But as Jake discovered, it didn't have to be this way.
sentences.zh: 但正如杰克所发现的，事情本不必如此。

sentences.en: I found a very old map that was put out as publicity
sentences.zh: 我找到了一张年代久远的宣传地图，

sentences.en: by the old Pacific Electric Railway that owned this massive electric railway system.
sentences.zh: 是曾经拥有庞大电气化铁路系统的老太平洋电车公司印制的。

sentences.en: And as part of their advertising,
sentences.zh: 作为他们广告宣传的一部分，

sentences.en: they had in huge letters the largest electric railway system in the world.
sentences.zh: 上面用醒目的大字写着“全世界最大的电气化铁路系统”。

sentences.en: And this flipped a switch in my head because this is Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 这一下子触动了我的神经，因为这里可是洛杉矶。

sentences.en: What Jake quickly learned is that L.A.
sentences.zh: 杰克很快了解到的是，洛杉矶

sentences.en: hasn't always been the car-centric city we know today.
sentences.zh: 并不一直都是我们今天所知道的汽车城市。

sentences.en: It was home to a massive public transit network.
sentences.zh: 它曾拥有庞大的公共交通网络。

sentences.en: At one time, Los Angeles, of all places,
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，在所有地方中，洛杉矶——

sentences.en: the land of freeways, traffic, and smog,
sentences.zh: 这个高速公路、交通拥堵和雾霾交织的土地，
竟然拥有一个电气化铁路系统，

sentences.en: that was four times the size of the modern London Underground.
sentences.zh: 其规模是现代伦敦地铁的四倍。

sentences.en: So I was thinking to myself, what happened here?
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就在想，这里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And so as I went down the rabbit hole,
I found that this was the common story in North America,
sentences.zh: 我发现这是北美普遍存在的故事，

sentences.en: like nowhere else in the world,
that the United States and Canada, to a lesser extent,
sentences.zh: 美国和加拿大（程度稍轻一些）

sentences.en: abandoned mass transit in a way that other industrialized countries didn't.
sentences.zh: 以其他工业化国家没有的方式放弃了公共交通。

sentences.en: This experience inspired Jake to write The Lost Subways of North America,
sentences.zh: 这段经历激励杰克写下了《北美失落的地铁》，

sentences.en: a book about the subways of our past, present, and future,
sentences.zh: 一本关于我们过去、现在和未来的地铁的书，

sentences.en: and why public transit in so many of our cities fall way short of our needs.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么我们那么多城市的公共交通远远无法满足需求。

sentences.en: In his book, Jake doesn't just write about subways.
sentences.zh: 在他的书中，杰克不只写了地铁。

sentences.en: He also looks at buses, streetcars, commuter rail,
sentences.zh: 他还研究了公交车、有轨电车、通勤铁路，

sentences.en: and basically all types of urban public transportation.
sentences.zh: 基本上涵盖了所有类型的城市公共交通。

sentences.en: And he says that for public transit to work in any city,
sentences.zh: 他说，要让公共交通在任何城市发挥作用，

sentences.en: it needs to have four main characteristics.
sentences.zh: 它需要具备四个主要特征。

sentences.en: That is, for anyone to actually use it.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，要让人真正愿意去坐。

sentences.en: A functioning transit system is fast, frequent, reliable,
sentences.zh: 一个运转良好的公交系统必须快速、频繁、可靠，

sentences.en: and it goes places people want to go.
sentences.zh: 并且能去到人们想去的地方。

sentences.en: So there are four ways to do it right.
sentences.zh: 所以要把这件事做好有四个方法。

sentences.en: According to Jake, though, there are many, many ways to do it wrong.
sentences.zh: 不过根据杰克的说法，做错的方法却有很多很多。

sentences.en: I like to think it's like that old line of Tolstoy's,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢借用托尔斯泰的那句老名言，

sentences.en: all happy transit systems are alike.
sentences.zh: 幸福的公交系统都是相似的。

sentences.en: Each unhappy transit system is unhappy in its own way.
sentences.zh: 不幸的公交系统各有各的不幸。

sentences.en: So in Miami, for instance, they have a metro system that is fast, frequent, and reliable,
sentences.zh: 比如在迈阿密，他们有一个快速、频繁且可靠的地铁系统，

sentences.en: but it doesn't go the places that people want to go.
sentences.zh: 但它却不到达人们想去的地方。

sentences.en: So very few people take the train.
In Philadelphia, they have a really excellent regional rail system
sentences.zh: 在费城，他们有一个非常出色的区域铁路系统，

sentences.en: run by SEPTA, which is the name of the Transit Authority.
sentences.zh: 由SEPTA运营，也就是交通管理局的名字。

sentences.en: And it goes all the places that people want to go.
sentences.zh: 它能到达人们想去的所有地方。

sentences.en: But they only run one train an hour,
sentences.zh: 但他们一小时只发一班车，

sentences.en: which makes a big difference in whether people are willing to take transit or not.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上决定了人们是否愿意选择公共交通。

sentences.en: The truth is, many North America's subway systems aren't just unhappy.
sentences.zh: 事实是，许多北美的地铁系统不仅仅是不幸。
它们简直是深刻而又令人沮丧地让人失望。

sentences.en: Because it's not like North American cities
sentences.zh: 因为这并不是说北美城市

sentences.en: haven't been trying to match the transit systems that you see in places like Western Europe or Japan.
sentences.zh: 没有努力去匹配你在西欧或日本等地看到的那些交通系统。

sentences.en: In fact, Jake's book points to time after time when we seemed to be just inches away
sentences.zh: 事实上，杰克的书一次又一次地指出，我们似乎曾数次离

sentences.en: from a robust, utopian future of fast, frequent, reliable, and convenient trains,
sentences.zh: 一个充满活力、乌托邦式的快速、频繁、可靠且便捷的列车未来只有咫尺之遥，

sentences.en: only to have one thing or a combination of things get in the way.
sentences.zh: 却偏偏因为这样或那样的原因（或种种因素的组合）而功亏一篑。

sentences.en: So all unhappy transit systems are unhappy in their own ways,
sentences.zh: 所以所有不幸的公交系统各有各的不幸，

sentences.en: but their particular failures and what we can learn from them
sentences.zh: 但它们各自的失败以及我们能从中吸取的教训

sentences.en: point to ways that maybe, just maybe,
sentences.zh: 指明了某种可能，哪怕只有一丝可能，

sentences.en: our cities can get the subways of our dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 我们的城市也能拥有梦想中的地铁。

sentences.en: Jake and I are going to go through a handful of North American cities
sentences.zh: 我和杰克将带大家回顾几个北美城市，
探讨究竟是哪里出了问题，

sentences.en: to find out what exactly makes or breaks a transit system.
sentences.zh: 从而弄清楚到底是什么因素决定了一个公交系统的成败。

sentences.en: Starting with the red car of Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 从洛杉矶的红色电车开始。

sentences.en: When Jake found the map that launched his research,
sentences.zh: 当杰克找到那张开启他研究的地图时，

sentences.en: what he was looking at was the route of L.A.'s red car.
sentences.zh: 他看到的是洛杉矶红色电车的路线。

sentences.en: Longtime 99PI listeners might remember our 2013 episode,
sentences.zh: 99PI的老听众可能还记得我们2013年的那一期节目，

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, the red car got Angelenos where they wanted to go.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪初，红色电车把洛杉矶人送到他们想去的地方。

sentences.en: It was a system of electric street trolleys
sentences.zh: 那是一个由电动街车组成的系统，

sentences.en: that connected seaside towns and suburban neighborhoods to downtown L.A.
sentences.zh: 将海滨城镇和郊区社区与洛杉矶市中心连接起来。

sentences.en: In its heyday, there were more than 2,100 trains running every day
sentences.zh: 在其鼎盛时期，每天有超过2,100辆列车在
长达1,000多英里的轨道上运行。

sentences.en: And the reason many Angelenos today have never even heard of the red car
sentences.zh: 而许多当今的洛杉矶人甚至从未听说过红色电车的原因，

sentences.en: has to do with monopoly, maintenance,
and the greed of a 20th century robber baron named Henry Huntington.
sentences.zh: 以及20世纪一个名叫亨利·亨廷顿的强盗大亨的贪婪有关。

sentences.en: Henry Huntington and his company, Pacific Electric,
sentences.zh: 亨利·亨廷顿和他的太平洋电车公司，

sentences.en: built the electric railway system that was the largest
sentences.zh: 构建了当时世界上最大、

sentences.en: and most impressive in the world at the time.
sentences.zh: 也最令人瞩目的电气化铁路系统。

sentences.en: But ironically enough, railways were not actually how Pacific Electric
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是，铁路实际上并不是太平洋电车
赚取大部分利润的方式。

sentences.en: In the United States and Canada, it was very common
sentences.zh: 在美国和加拿大，非常普遍

sentences.en: and quite frankly the norm for ostensibly a train company
sentences.zh: 且坦白说也是常态的是，一个表面上的铁路公司

sentences.en: to have another line of business where they made their real money.
sentences.zh: 往往还有另一条真正赚钱的业务线。

sentences.en: So in Seattle, it was Seattle Electric.
sentences.zh: 所以在西雅图，它是西雅图电力公司。

sentences.en: In Atlanta, it was Georgia Power,
sentences.zh: 在亚特兰大，它是佐治亚电力公司，

sentences.en: which still is the power company in Atlanta,
sentences.zh: 它至今仍然是亚特兰大的电力公司，

sentences.en: that ran the trains because those two businesses worked together really well at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时这两项业务配合得非常好，所以它运营着列车。

sentences.en: If you wanted to electrify a neighborhood,
sentences.zh: 如果你想让一个社区实现电气化，

sentences.en: you could also run a train line out to that neighborhood
sentences.zh: 你也可以顺便修一条铁路线到那个社区，

sentences.en: and kill two birds with one stone.
So it was pretty common for power companies to have a subway side hustle.
sentences.zh: 所以电力公司兼营地铁副业是相当普遍的。

sentences.en: And in the case of Pacific Electric,
sentences.zh: 就太平洋电车公司而言，

sentences.en: that side hustle was all in the interest of making money on real estate.
sentences.zh: 这个副业完全是为了在房地产上赚钱。

sentences.en: Henry Huntington bought up a bunch of farmland.
sentences.zh: 亨利·亨廷顿买下了大片农田。

sentences.en: He turned that farmland into suburbs and then he made those suburbs desirable
sentences.zh: 他把这些农田变成郊区，然后通过把它们与——你猜对了——火车连接起来，

sentences.en: and valuable by connecting them with, you guessed it, trains.
sentences.zh: 让这些郊区变得令人向往且极具价值。

sentences.en: All through the early 20th century, Pacific Electric just kept going like this.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪初，太平洋电车就这样一直运营下去。

sentences.en: Henry Huntington would buy up land, run a train through it,
sentences.zh: 亨利·亨廷顿买下土地，通上火车，

sentences.en: sell that land for profit, and then do it all over again.
sentences.zh: 把土地卖掉获利，然后周而复始。

sentences.en: And as the red car routes got longer,
sentences.zh: 随着红色电车路线越来越长，

sentences.en: LA's sprawling suburbs started to take shape,
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶蔓延的郊区开始成形，

sentences.en: even before most Angelenos owned a car.
sentences.zh: 甚至在大多数洛杉矶人拥有汽车之前就已经如此了。

sentences.en: If you look at the maps of the old Pacific Electric system,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看老太平洋电车系统的地图，

sentences.en: you can tie that to the great streets of LA.
sentences.zh: 你就能把它与洛杉矶的大街联系起来。

sentences.en: Santa Monica Boulevard and Sunset Boulevard had trains at one time,
sentences.zh: 圣莫尼卡大道和日落大道曾经都有火车通车，

sentences.en: and all of the neighborhoods that were built up around there
sentences.zh: 所有围绕这些地方建设的社区，
都是围绕着火车来设计的。

sentences.en: Even places deep into the suburbs, like San Marino, right?
sentences.zh: 甚至像圣马力诺这样深入郊区的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: These are places that were originally designed to be accessed via train.
sentences.zh: 这些地方最初就是设计成通过火车才能到达的。

sentences.en: This may sound like an alternate, better version of LA that could have been.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能像是洛杉矶本可以拥有的另一个更好的版本。
一个对公共交通友好的洛杉矶，

sentences.en: one in which Jake never had to languish behind that Jeep
sentences.zh: 一个杰克永远不必在高速公路上

sentences.en: with too many bumper stickers on the freeway.
sentences.zh: 那一辆贴满车贴的吉普车后面苦苦苦熬的洛杉矶。

sentences.en: But the people actually using the red car didn't feel that way.
sentences.zh: 但真正使用红色电车的人并不这么觉得。

sentences.en: Even though it went to a lot of places people wanted to go,
sentences.zh: 尽管它通往许多人们想去的地方，

sentences.en: the cracks began to show by the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪20年代，裂痕开始显现。

sentences.en: The trains were falling into disrepair.
And that's because the red car itself didn't make money.
sentences.zh: 这是因为红色电车本身并不赚钱。

sentences.en: It was just a convenient way to inflate property values.
sentences.zh: 它只是推高房产价值的一种便捷方式。

sentences.en: Henry Huntington didn't care about how well it was running.
sentences.zh: 亨利·亨廷顿根本不在乎它的运营状况如何。

sentences.en: So once the real estate ventures began to run out of cheap land,
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦房地产投资开始耗尽廉价土地，

sentences.en: there was no reason to keep running good passenger service.
sentences.zh: 就没有理由继续提供良好的客运服务了。

sentences.en: And for a 20-year period between like 1925 and World War II,
sentences.zh: 在大约从1925年到二战的20年时间里，

sentences.en: the Pacific Electric's passenger services were bleeding money
sentences.zh: 太平洋电车的客运服务一直在严重亏损，

sentences.en: because the company didn't particularly care
sentences.zh: 因为公司并不怎么在意，

sentences.en: and they were making their real money
by transporting freight and building homes.
sentences.zh: 是通过货运运输和建造房屋。

sentences.en: The final blow came with the rise of cars,
sentences.zh: 致命的打击随着汽车的兴起而到来，

sentences.en: which shared space with the street trolleys
sentences.zh: 汽车与有轨电车共享道路空间，

sentences.en: and slowed them down even more.
sentences.zh: 并进一步降低了它们的速度。

sentences.en: Eventually, Pacific Electric was losing so much money
sentences.zh: 最终，太平洋电车损失惨重，

sentences.en: that the company had to ask for public dollars
sentences.zh: 以至于公司不得不请求公共资金

sentences.en: But by this time, Angelino's absolutely hated Pacific Electric
sentences.zh: 但到了这个时候，洛杉矶人已经极其厌恶太平洋电车

sentences.en: The City Council of Los Angeles said,
we're not doing this because the public doesn't want it.
sentences.zh: 我们不会这么做，因为公众不希望这样。
经过20年糟糕透顶的服务

sentences.en: and their reputation of commercial ruthlessness
sentences.zh: 以及其一向唯利是图的商业名声

sentences.en: had really soured the public on public transport as an institution.
sentences.zh: 确实让公众对公共交通这种基础设施彻底寒了心。

sentences.en: The result of all this is that L.A.
sentences.zh: 这一切导致的结果是，洛杉矶
成了一座以汽车为中心的城市，

sentences.en: even if it does have a modest regional subway today.
sentences.zh: 尽管它如今确实拥有一个规模不大的区域地铁网。

sentences.en: As for the red car, it limped along through the 1940s and 50s
sentences.zh: 至于红色电车，它在20世纪40和50年代步履维艰地维持着

sentences.en: until finally, in 1961, it ran for the last time.
sentences.zh: 直到1961年，终于迎来了它的末班车。

sentences.en: Some of the trolley cars got shipped abroad to live a second life,
sentences.zh: 有些电车被运往海外以开启第二春，

sentences.en: but most of them were sold for scrap.
sentences.zh: 但大多数都被当成废铁卖掉了。

sentences.en: This is in contrast to another North American city on our list,
sentences.zh: 这与我们榜单上的另一座北美城市形成了鲜明对比，

sentences.en: which today has a booming public transit system,
sentences.zh: 那座城市如今拥有一个蓬勃发展的公共交通系统，

sentences.en: a city whose subways aren't lost per se,
sentences.zh: 那里的地铁与其说是消失了，

sentences.en: but are completely painfully hobbled by good old-fashioned bureaucracy.
sentences.zh: 不如说是被陈旧的官僚作风折腾得痛苦不堪、步履维艰。

sentences.en: One of the most famous transit systems in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国最著名的交通系统之一

sentences.en: is, of course, the New York City subway.
New York's Metropolitan Transit Authority, or MTA,
sentences.zh: 纽约的大都会运输署，即MTA，

sentences.en: has the largest and busiest subway system on the continent.
sentences.zh: 拥有北美最大、最繁忙的地铁系统。

sentences.en: And whether you love it or hate it, you ride the subway.
sentences.zh: 不管你是爱它还是恨它，你都得坐地铁。

sentences.en: It's something that needs to be there.
sentences.zh: 它是那种必须存在的东西。

sentences.en: And New York cannot function without a working subway.
sentences.zh: 而且没有正常运转的地铁，纽约就无法运转。

sentences.en: By and large, for over a century,
sentences.zh: 总的来说，一个多世纪以来，

sentences.en: New York's transit system has stood as a shining example of what works.
sentences.zh: 纽约的交通系统一直是成功典范的耀眼灯塔。

sentences.en: It's the one place where you're usually better off taking the train
sentences.zh: 这是唯一一个通常坐火车比

sentences.en: as opposed to driving to get from point A to point B.
sentences.zh: 开车从A点到B点要好得多地方。

sentences.en: A big reason for this success is that most of New York's subway system
sentences.zh: 这种成功的一个主要原因在于，纽约大部分的地铁系统

sentences.en: was built pretty quickly and efficiently.
sentences.zh: 都是相当迅速且高效地建成的。

sentences.en: The first New York subway line started getting built in the year 1900,
sentences.zh: 纽约第一条地铁线于1900年开始兴建，

sentences.en: and by the time it opened in 1904,
the train ran from City Hall downtown all the way to Harlem.
sentences.zh: 列车从市中心的市政厅一路开到了哈莱姆。

sentences.en: By 1940, the New York subway system had over 400 stations.
sentences.zh: 到1940年，纽约地铁系统已经拥有400多个车站。

sentences.en: But by the mid-20th century, after going through a series of mergers,
sentences.zh: 但在20世纪中叶，在经历了一系列兼并、
